rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods <U+2013> three-season (2006/07<U+2013>2008/09) split-plot field experiment at Daxing, NCP, comparing level-basin (BI) and surface drip (DI) irrigation at four scheduling levels, with flow-meter measured irrigation amounts, TDR/gravimetric soil water, yield and WUE. Q2: Results, Table 4 and Table 9 <U+2013> irrigation amounts measured per treatment; relative to level-basin B1, drip treatments D1 and D2 saved 14<U+2013>19% of irrigation water with only 5<U+2013>8% yield decrease, and D3/D4 saved 35%; abstract and conclusions state DI improved WUE and could produce expected yields with less water than BI.
rows.notes: Comparator is level-basin (surface) irrigation, which is close to the 'flood irrigation' in the passage; crop is wheat, matching the claim. Savings reported (14<U+2013>35%) are below the 'up to 50%' in the passage. Q3: irrigation amounts measured by a single method (flow meter); no second independent method. Q4: ETc was lower under DI (water balance, Table 4/8) and soil water was monitored, but the stated mechanism for water saving (uniform application, lower soil evaporation) is only asserted ('could be'), soil evaporation was not measured, and ETc is derived from a water balance that includes the applied irrigation plus assumed application efficiencies (90% DI, 80% BI) and an assumed drainage coefficient; judged not an independent measurement of the intermediate variable. Q5/Q6: single site, single crop, 4.5<U+00D7>5 m plots. Q7: the advantage in yield/WUE is reported 'under deficit irrigation conditions' and the recommendation is qualified by 'without irrigation system investment consideration', but these are not stated as requirements for the water-saving effect itself. Q8: only limitation stated concerns LAI measurement on small plots, not the water-saving result; assumed efficiencies/wetted fractions and drainage coefficient are not acknowledged as limitations. Q9: only means and Duncan letter groupings; no SD, SE, CI or range for irrigation savings.

notes: Full text appears complete. Study is a 3-year plot experiment with winter wheat only; results on water saving are percentages relative to the fullest level-basin treatment (B1).
